skin.repairLog:
skin check still fails after repair: SKIN_STRETCH, SKIN_BIND_MISMATCH
Bind-pose mismatch on bone_28: the mesh was modelled in a different pose than the skeleton assumes. Weight smoothing and triangle cuts only mask it. For a recognised humanoid run repair-skin --rebuild-limbs (rebuilds the legs in the skeleton's pose); otherwise rebuild the limbs in your DCC tool or regenerate and re-rig the model in the pose the skeleton assumes.
Still failing after smooth-bridges: SKIN_STRETCH, SKIN_BIND_MISMATCH. Cutting stretched triangles opens holes; prefer --rebuild-limbs or re-rigging.
Re-admit the repaired file with `aura3d assets add` (it gets a new hash); do not edit the manifest by hand.

mocapRepairReverted.reason: Real-GPU QA: the repair-skin pass (weight smoothing, normalize/prune, --cut-stretch holes) shredded hands and straps and opened see-through holes although its stretch count fell. Shipped weights are the generator's own (bit-identical POSITION/JOINTS_0/WEIGHTS_0/indices); the game limits arm elevation (100 deg) and forearm/wrist twist (75/60 deg) instead.

revertedRepair.clips: fal text-to-motion clips (tools/idol/motion-specs/bunker-zero.json) baked from the shipped pose code
revertedRepair.command: aura3d assets repair-skin --keep-clips <those clips> --refit-skeleton --normalize --prune-distant --smooth-bridges --smooth-threshold 1.25 --smooth-rounds 12 --smooth-rings 6 --cut-stretch 4 (from the unrepaired Idol GLB)
revertedRepair.note: Skeleton unchanged (refit moved 0 joints); weights smoothed, triangles past 4x removed. Only the idle clip is stored; the game drives the bones from code.

doubleSided.reason: Real-GPU / CPU-skinned QA: skin folds at extreme generated-motion poses and single-sided cloth showed back faces, which back-face culling turned into see-through holes. Materials are double-sided (cull none) and opaque.
